title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: GAR — posterity 'sinned in another' as Christ-satisfaction analogy
pass_a_gloss: Satisfying and having satisfaction imputed are far apart. Yet when theologians say we satisfied in Christ they mean only that his satisfaction is imputed through union with him as spiritual head, so God reckons us as if we had satisfied.
pass_b_english: So for someone to satisfy, and for satisfaction to be imputed to someone, are surely far diverse. And yet when the theologians teach that we have satisfied in Christ, they mean nothing else than that Christ's satisfaction is imputed to us. Or that Christ exhibited that satisfaction which, because of the union which we have with him as our spiritual and mystical head, is imputed to us, so that before God we are held as if we ourselves had satisfied through ourselves.
source_text: Sic satisfacere aliquem, & alicui satisfactionem imputari, sunt sane longe diversa, & tamen cum docent Theologi nos in Christo satisfecisse, non aliud sibi volunt, quam Christi satisfactionem nobis imputari, sive Christum eam satisfactionem exhibuisse, quae propter unionem, quam cum eo habemus tanquam capite nostro spirituali & mystico, nobis imputetur, ita ut apud Deum habeamur, quasi ipsi per nos satisfecissemus.

choices.choice: Christ-satisfaction talk is imputation-via-union, offered as parallel
